extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, engineers, and technical professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for evaluating scientific books, reference works, expedition/field reports, and policy/technical conference reports — focusing on usefulness, accuracy, comprehensiveness, practicality, and impartiality. Intended to guide critical appraisal and review in a scientific journal context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of the metric system and completeness of conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Author’s object is to explain the metric system and to state in full how to convert from the English units to metric units, and vice versa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion material should fully state conversion procedures and be exhaustive in conversion tables so the work is practically useful (the reviewer: "The conversion tables are very exhaustive."). Target utility for industrial/workshop users is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account of measuring devices for accurate measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an account of the vernier and other devices used by engineers for accurate measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical descriptions of measuring instruments that are directly useful to engineers strengthen the book’s applicability; inclusion of illustrative charts/plates is a plus (page notes "excellent account of the vernier and other devices").

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and avoidance of prejudice in ethnographic description
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid allowing the author’s prejudice to colour the narrative when describing native customs (criticised: author 'rarely fails to stigmatise them as "degrading," "disgusting," or worse').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethnographic treatments should be sympathetic but impartial; reviewers flag overt stigmatizing language and requirement for balanced, objective presentation. Prejudice that obscures facts reduces scholarly value and may require additional scholarly context to disentangle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and usefulness of cultural/folklore collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a full and careful account of the culture; collect and present folk-lore in an interesting and useful way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections should be comprehensive enough to be of use to those wishing to study native customs; major topics (e.g., fetishism, secret societies) should be treated thoroughly and with clear sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanise subject-matter without undue popularisation
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt to 'humanise Elementary Physics without popularising it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strike a balance: make the material engaging and relatable (connect pupil’s experience with principles) while preserving theoretical rigor. Readability and educational value are assessed together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasise theory; restrict experiments to principle-illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Theory has been given the main prominence. Experiments have not been described unless to elucidate principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For instructional texts aimed at pupils/teachers, focus on conceptual clarity; include experiments only insofar as they illuminate principles. Frequent historical references and illustrative portraits may reinforce learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency, careful revision, and incorporation of latest data
rubrics_metrics.description: Material should be thoroughly revised and tables of constants 'brought into accord with the best data obtainable'; include recent important work (e.g., Siegbahn, Aston, Rutherford, Bohr).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works and manuals must update constants and cite contemporary discoveries/theories; systematic coverage of recent developments makes a volume recommendable to readers seeking up-to-date accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct theoretical application and numerical accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply theoretical formulae correctly; numerical results must account for all relevant factors (example: intensity of sound reflection depends on refractive index and relative densities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should verify that derivations use correct parameters (e.g., include density ratios when evaluating sound transmission) and distinguish effects due to reflection versus absorption. Cite prior foundational work when relevant (e.g., Lord Rayleigh).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough taxonomic/reporting practice in field studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specimen counts, collection locality and date, state of specimens, and comparisons with type material (example: 'I examined twenty-three specimens... Not one of them differed...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field/collection reports should record numbers, condition, morphological comparisons, synonymy notes, and any parasitic or ecological observations. These details are essential for extending knowledge and for future verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost‑effectiveness and reduction of administrative burden (policy proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a proposed patent scheme materially reduces the number of separate applications and the cost and procedural complexity facing inventors (current burden cited: 'not less than forty-six separate applications... cost... more than three hundred pounds... additional sum of twelve hundred pounds').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy proposals should be evaluated on practical savings to users, simplicity of procedure, and whether they genuinely encourage inventive activity by lowering friction and expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve autonomy of local jurisdictions in empire-wide schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: While an Empire Patent may be desirable, preserve the autonomy of the self-governing Dominions and of India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schemes that centralise authority must be judged against the need to respect local legislative autonomy and practical constraints (distance, delay). Retention of local patent offices was argued as preferable to wholesale centralisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a meaningful examination for novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid schemes that abolish compulsory examination into novelty (criticised scheme: would result in abolition of existing compulsory examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any acceptable patent scheme should include adequate examination/search procedures to ensure novelty; weakening or removing novelty examination reduces patent quality and is a major objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local registration with opportunity for opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: To make a patent operative in any country, registration in that country is compulsory, and registration should be open to opposition where local law permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empire‑wide mechanisms should coexist with local registration systems and preserve local opposition rights and judicial remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include practitioners' input and oral evidence in policy formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not exclude oral evidence from outside bodies; practitioners 'who are in daily contact with such matters' must be heard (example: Chartered Institute of Patent Agents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and procedural complexity demands consultation with experienced practitioners to produce workable schemes; excluding such evidence risks producing impractical outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish substantive law from procedural mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be necessary to distinguish between the law to be applied when the patent is granted and the procedure for obtaining the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy design should separately address substantive legal rules (rights conferred, scope) and procedural steps (filing, examination, registration), since conflating them leads to confusion in implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh expense against benefits; prefer practicable schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate schemes on expense and expected beneficial results (one plan: large expenditure with great advantages; another: small expenditure with diminished results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select proposals that attain a reasonable balance of achievable benefits relative to administrative and capital costs; impracticable but ideal schemes may be rejected for lack of feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritativeness and calibre of contributors in reference works
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference work's value depends on 'authoritativeness, the maturity of judgment, the originality and inviting freshness of treatment which are exhibited by the majority of the writers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should recruit accepted authorities and experienced investigators; reviewers value known experts and judge articles partly on contributors’ reputations and demonstrated expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of topical coverage in encyclopedic/reference volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to cover the entire range of physics and the applications of physics to industry; Volume 1 covers mechanics, engineering, and heat (some fifty articles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference works should aim for breadth across relevant subfields and practical applications; include multiple articles on major subtopics (calorimetry, dynamical similarity, steam engineering, internal combustion, friction, lubrication, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include discussion of future trends and note omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers expect authors to indicate the future trend of their subjects; omission noted: 'one would have liked to know something of the writers’ views on the future trend of their subjects.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference articles benefit from a forward-looking perspective (possible technological developments such as gas turbines, aircraft/locomotive applications). Reviewers call out notable omissions that affect usefulness to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical clarity and usefulness for engineers/practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the work helps engineers 'turn physical principles to account' — practical orientation and co-operation between physicist and engineer are essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise applied explanations, examples, and practical measurement/experimental methods (e.g., electrical methods of calorimetry emphasized because electrical energy is easy to measure). Usability by practitioners is a major evaluation axis.
